claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 1. `src/sqllens/config.py` now sets `extra="forbid"` on the `[agent]` section (line 457) while `_RETIRED_AGENT_KEYS` (line 444) forgives only `show_memory_details`, so the retired `show_sql` key becomes a start-up failure instead of being ignored. `docs/external/release-notes.md:83` tells operators the opposite in writing: "an unrenamed `show_sql` key is silently ignored, so the new default-on behavior will be in effect regardless." `show_sql` was a real, documented `[agent]` key shipped in the May 18, 2026 release (`docs/external/release-notes.md:93`). An operator whose `sqllens.toml` still carries `show_sql`, or who still exports `SQLLENS_AGENT__SHOW_SQL`, now gets a `ValidationError` from `sqllens validate` and `sqllens serve` rather than a running server. This is the exact outcome the new comment at `src/sqllens/config.py:462-464` says strictness must not produce. Adding `show_sql` to `_RETIRED_AGENT_KEYS` fixes it; the three places that state the retired-key list is complete — `docs/external/configuration.md`, `changelog.d/360.changed.md` and `docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md` — then need the second key named too.
